pow.signature: Exactly two finite binary64 Number operands; the result is Number and is nullable exactly when either operand is nullable. Untyped NULL takes the unique Number signature. No implicit conversion, distinct INT64, NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC or non-finite overload is admitted.
pow.value: Return the first operand raised to the second. With non-null operands, a negative base requires an integral exponent, tested in binary64 without narrowing to a bounded integer. Either sign of zero with a negative exponent fails with the existing arithmetic failure. Zero to zero is one. A non-finite result from finite inputs fails with the existing arithmetic failure. Preserve representable subnormal results and return canonical positive zero for unrepresentable underflow or either zero sign. Either NULL operand produces NULL after both child evaluations succeed, before validating these value-domain rules.

Identical admitted inputs and selected semantic contracts preserve exact logical Number bits across targets; no live-BigQuery last-bit equivalence is claimed.
pow.evaluation: Evaluate the base then exponent exactly once when demanded, including the second child after a NULL result. Apply strict NULL only after both child evaluations succeed. Preserve child failures, enclosing lazy demand, first-failure order, cancellation and existing logical work, frame, workspace and live-value budgets. Reuse the canonical binary scalar evaluator; do not reevaluate children or add a frontend evaluator.
